THE HEADLINES: 

  1. Centre to reconvene Lok Sabha on 30th November and Rajya Sabha on 2nd December to transact essential government business.
  2. President Droupadi Murmu calls for Indianness in institutional work culture; Urges citizens to take pride in their heritage and shed colonial mindset on Constitution Day.
  3. Several countries reaffirm solidarity with India in combating terrorism as Nation pays tributes to victims of 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks.
  4. Colombo Security Conclave members including Maldives, India, Mauritius and Sri Lanka reaffirm collective commitment to promote regional peace and security.
  5. IFFI pays tribute to late actor Nana Patekar with special screening of restored Hindi film Diksha.
  6. In Cricket, India A set a target of 318 runs against Sri Lanka A in first Semi-Final of Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament in Doha.

The Government has requested Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla to reconvene the sitting of Lok Sabha on Monday to transact essential Government Business. In a social media post, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said Rajya Sabha Chairman CP Radhakrishnan has been requested to reconvene the Upper House on 2nd of December. The Minister said that subject to exigencies of the Business, the sitting of both Houses may conclude on the 3rd of December.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

President Droupadi Murmu has said that the Indian judiciary has continued to uphold and strengthen the fundamental ideals of justice while adapting to changing circumstances and expectations. Addressing Constitution Day celebrations organised by the Supreme Court in New Delhi this evening, President Murmu said, the timely delivery of justice is an essential component of the very concept of justice. She said, to ensure that justice is accessible in a timely manner, the judiciary is undertaking various initiatives such as simplifying procedures, leveraging technology, and establishing special courts. The President noted that despite these efforts, the massive backlog of pending cases remains a significant challenge for the country’s justice delivery system. She expressed confidence that this challenge will be addressed through the concerted efforts being made at every level of the judiciary.

 

 

The President said, Indianness should be reflected in every dimension of the working culture of the institutions of the country. She said, over the past few years, there has been significant momentum in efforts to take pride in our heritage and free ourselves from the colonial mindset. President Murmu said, in keeping with the philosophy of replacing punishment with justice, the Indian Judiciary is strengthening the implementation of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita as an instrument for ensuring speedy justice. In his address, Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant highlighted several institutional reforms aimed at improving access to justice. He said that fresh matters are now listed automatically, while cases involving personal liberty and urgent interim relief must reach a Bench within two working days.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah said that all BJP-ruled states will implement the Uniform Civil Code (UCC), asserting that laws should not be framed on the basis of religion. Addressing Sambvidhan Gaurav Divas in New Delhi this evening, he said that the framers of the Constitution had included the UCC in the Directive Principles of State Policy and envisioned a uniform law for every citizen. Mr Shah further said, India had witnessed several transfers of power without bloodshed, with each transition taking place in accordance with the constitutional process.

 

 

Amit Shah has said that Constitution is not merely a guidebook for governance but a document reflecting the hopes, aspirations and values of the nation.

 

 

Taking a dig at the Opposition, the Minister urged its leaders to examine the original copy of the Constitution to understand its spirit. 

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Several diplomatic missions in India today paid tribute to the victims of the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks, while reaffirming their solidarity with India in combating terrorism. The United States Ambassador to India, Sergio Gor, paid tribute to the 166 people killed in the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks, including six Americans, reaffirming Washington’s support for India in combating terrorism. In a social media post, Gor said, their law enforcement partnership remains vital to bringing terrorists to justice. Marking the 18th anniversary of the horrific terror attacks, the French Embassy remembered those killed, including two French nationals. It also recalled French President Emmanuel Macron’s tribute to the victims during his visit to India, while reaffirming solidarity with New Delhi in the fight against terrorism. Israel has also said it stands firmly with India in the joint fight against terror as it honoured the memory of the victims of the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia today said that department of posts has recorded nearly 16 percent growth in financial year 2025-26, with its annual revenue increasing from around 13 thousand 200 crore rupees to nearly 15 thousand 500 crore rupees. Addressing a press briefing in New Delhi, Mr Scindia said the department aims to achieve revenue of over 19 thousand 800 crore rupees in the current financial year. The Minister noted that the government aims to transform the Department of Posts from a cost centre into a profit centre by 2030. 

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav today released the party’s manifesto for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in Lucknow. The manifesto is titled ‘Jan-Man Ka Manifesto’ with the slogan ‘Sattais Ka Sankalp, PDA Ka Prannpatra’.  The manifesto outlines proposals on employment, education, healthcare, agriculture, workers, governance and infrastructure. The manifesto promises recruitment to vacant government posts in time-bound manner, transparent hiring and scholarships, skill training, financial support for education abroad and help for start-ups. Party also promises old pension scheme in its  election manifesto. The Manifesto promises a 100 per cent waiver of farmers’ outstanding electricity bills within three months of forming the govt, free power for agricultural irrigation and up to 300 units of free domestic electricity.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Member states of Colombo Security Conclave (CSC) have reaffirmed the collective commitment to promote regional peace and security through sustained cooperation. The 8th National Security Advisor Level Meeting of the Colombo Security Conclave was hosted by Maldives yesterday. External Affairs Ministry said in a statement that the Member States placed emphasis on strengthening collaboration across the five pillars of cooperation, particularly through training, sharing best practices and capacity-building initiatives, while underlining the importance of continued collective efforts towards advancing the objectives of the Colombo Security Conclave. The high-level delegations were led by National Security Advisor Ajit Doval. The CSC Member states including Maldives, India, Mauritius and Sri Lanka signed the Agreed Minutes and adopted the Roadmap of Cooperation for 2026-2027, setting out key deliverables and planned activities under the five pillars of cooperation.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar held a meeting with Foreign Minister of Seychelles, Barry Faure in New Delhi. They reaffirmed the shared commitment to further strengthening people-centric partnership focussing on health, connectivity, skilling, energy, cyber and AI. Both Ministers also discussed cooperation in the Indian Ocean Rim Association, IORA and regional issues. India will host the IORA Council of Ministers Meeting tomorrow.The theme for India’s IORA chairship 2025-2027 is “Innovation, Openness, Resilience and Adaptability in the Indian Ocean Region”. The External Affairs Minister also met his Mauritius counterpart Dhananjay Ramful and reviewed key areas of bilateral relationship, including progress under the Special Economic Package.

 

 

The IORA Meetings are slated to deliberate on future policy direction for IORA with an emphasis on reviewing regional cooperation frameworks and identifying new areas of collaboration.

Kuwait’s Ministry of Defence has reported that they had to deal with multiple drone attacks today. The spokesperson for the Ministry stated the armed forces detected a number of hostile drones inside Kuwaiti airspace today and dealt with them. The official statement added that the Iranians targeted a vital Kuwaiti site, causing shrapnel to fall – resulting in the death of 2 Italian nationals, while 2 more persons were injured.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

The 57th International Film Festival of India  marked its seventh day in Goa with tributes to cinematic legends, masterclasses and special film screenings. The festival today paid homage to late actor Nana Patekar. Mukesh Chhabra conducted a masterclass titled ‘The Casting Magic: Auditions Unplugged and ICFT Jury Highlighted Cinema’s Role in Promoting Peace at IFFI. More details from our correspondent.

 

 

“IFFI paid tribute to actor Nana Patekar today with a special screening of the restored Hindi film Diksha. Acclaimed casting director Mukesh Chhabra conducted a masterclass titled ‘The Casting Magic: Auditions Unplugged. Chhabra spoke about how actors are chosen for films.

 

 

Another session by Natalie Wade of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences gave participants an insight into how film entries and the voting process works in Oscars. Meanwhile, the ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal jury discussed cinema’s role in promoting peace and understanding. Ten films, including three Indian are competing for the award. Next 2 days of the festival are going to be equally interesting. Mahesh for Akashvani News, Panaji.”

In Cricket, chasing a target of 318 runs set by India A, Sri Lanka A were 169 for no loss in 21 overs against India A in the first Semi-Final of Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament in Doha, when reports last came in. Opting to bat first, India A scored 317 runs losing 8 wickets in stipulated 50 overs. For India A, Abhishek Sharma scored highest 78 runs off 63 balls.

Defending champions and top seeds India’s Gayatri Gopichand and Treesa Jolly continued their winning run to enter the quarter-finals of the Syed Modi India International HSBC World Tour Super 300 Badminton Championships.

 

 

In women’s singles, four Indian shuttlers, including last year’s semi-finalists Unnati Hooda and Tanvi Sharma, advanced to the quarter-finals. Anmol Kharb and Tasnim Mir also registered an impressive upset victories to progress to the next round.

The government has approved six new urea plants in brownfield category under the National Investment Policy for Urea-2026, with an investment of approximately 54 thousand crore rupees. The move aims to strengthen agricultural resilience, ensure fertiliser security and achieve self-reliance in urea production. The six projects are MFL-Madras in Tamil Nadu, NFL-Nangal in Punjab, KFL-Shahjahanpur in Uttar Pradesh, Matix-Panagarh in West Bengal, CFCL-Gadepan in Rajasthan and IIPL-Jagdishpur in Uttar Pradesh. The Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilisers said, each brownfield project involves an estimated capital investment of around nine thousand crore rupees. The projects are expected to advance India’s journey towards self-reliance in urea production while generating employment opportunities.

The Union Cabinet today approved a Scheme for the Enhancement of the Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE) Manufacturing Ecosystem, with a total outlay of 11 thousand crore rupees. Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw briefed the media in New Delhi this afternoon on the decisions taken during the Cabinet meeting. The Minister said, the scheme aims to incentivise domestic manufacturing of construction and infrastructure equipment and its components.

Mr Vaishnaw said, in another major decision, the Cabinet has given nod to the development of a second container terminal at Kamarajar Port Limited in Tamil Nadu.

Welcoming the decision, Prime Minister Narendra Modi in a social media post said, the second container terminal at Kamarajar Port in Tamil Nadu will reduce dependence on foreign ports and enhance the competitiveness of India’s exports.

Mr Vaishnaw said, the government also cleared the development of a Greenfield Airport at Doloo at Silchar in Assam, at an estimated cost of two thousand 14 crore rupees.

Hailing the Cabinet’s decision, Prime Minister Modi said the proposed airport in Silchar will significantly improve air connectivity in South Assam and adjoining states. He said the project would also give a major boost to trade, tea and agro-based industries, while creating new opportunities in tourism, investment and employment.

In another decision, the Cabinet approved the continuation of the Postal Operations Scheme for the financial year 2026-27 to 2030-31. The scheme aims to modernise the postal network, strengthen mail and parcel operations, improve rural connectivity and enhance citizen-centric services. It also approved the continuation of the Estates Management Scheme for the Department of Posts. It aims to comprehensively modernise the estates infrastructure of the Department of Posts.

India and China continue to engage in diplomatic and military-level talks to maintain peace and stability along the Line of Actual Control (LAC). External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated this while addressing the media in New Delhi this evening. Mr Jaiswal informed that a meeting of senior military commanders was held recently in the Eastern Sector.

On incidents of violence against minorities in Bangladesh, the spokesperson said India is concerned about such developments. He urged the Bangladesh government to conduct thorough investigations and bring those responsible to justice.           

On the extradition request concerning former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, Mr Jaiswal said the matter is being examined in accordance with established procedures. He clarified that the case of an individual willing to return voluntarily to her country on a travel document is separate from the extradition request.
On the show-cause notice issued to CJP’s Saurav Das, Mr Jaiswal said, passport applicants are required to provide accurate information. He informed that, based on reports received from the concerned law enforcement authorities, the Regional Passport Office in Chennai had issued a show-cause notice to Mr Das, seeking clarification within seven days regarding his place of birth. The spokesperson added that Mr Das had also been advised not to use his passport until he submits his response.

The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa today witnessed the successful conclusion of 20th edition of WAVES Film Bazaar, international film premieres and musical tributes. A special masterclass was also held paying tribute to legendary playback singers Lata Mangeshkar, Asha Bhosle and S. Janaki, celebrating their timeless contribution to Indian music and cinema.
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting said, today two Letters of Intent for Indo-Chile co-productions have also been signed at the WAVES Film Bazaar, while 14 MoUs and agreements are nearing finalisation following business interactions at the five-day marketplace. We have a report:

“The Additional Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting Shri Prabhat, informed that WAVES Film Bazaar by NFDC, brought 471 buyers from 54 countries, leading to Fourteen MoUs. film Skylark from Kyrgyzstan, directed by Narghiza Dotieva, premiered in the International Competition section. It explores the impact of border disputes on a teenager. Ecuadorian filmmaker Verenice Benítez’s Nunkui made its Asia Premiere in the Mission Life section. The film explores the relationship between an Amazonian community and nature amid threats from mining activities. Renowned playback singer K. S. Chithra, during the Lata Mangeshkar talk recalled the influence of the three legendary singers Lata Mangeshkar, S. Janaki and Asha Bhosale on her musical journey. Mahesh CHOPDE, Akashvani News, Panaji.”

Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has said, women’s safety, dignity and economic independence must go hand in hand with development. The Minister was speaking at the launch of the fifth edition of the national gender equality campaign, ‘Nayi Chetna – Pahal Badlav Ki’, in New Delhi today. Mr Chouhan highlighted the important role of women-led Self-Help Groups in taking awareness and support mechanisms to the grassroots.

<><><> 

Political parties have stepped up preparations for the upcoming Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh. BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary today held a meeting with former office-bearers of the party organisation in Sant Kabir Nagar. The meeting focused on strengthening the party organisation from the booth to the mandal level and reviewing the Special Summary Revision campaign.
Meanwhile, the Samajwadi Party, amid ongoing seat-sharing discussions with the Congress, announced candidates for five Assembly constituencies.

The Supreme Court today said it will hear, within a day or two, applications seeking directions for the lighting of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp at Deepathoon atop Thiruparankundram Hill in Madurai district of Tamil Nadu. The development comes a day after the annual Karthigai Deepam lamp was lit at its customary location at Uchipillayar Mandapam, but not at the stone pillar atop the hill, as directed by the Apex Court.
Meanwhile, the Tamil Nadu government today apologised to the Supreme Court over the failure to light the ceremonial lamp at the disputed Deepathoon. The state government attributed the situation to the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy Temple authorities, alleging that they had not authorised the team proposed to carry out the exercise.

<><><> 

The fifth edition of Kashi Tamil Sangamam will be held in Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh from 28th of November to 12th of December. It will focus on the theme – Thirukkural Payilvom – Thirukkural Abhyas Karen, promoting the timeless teachings of the Thirukkural among young learners. The Thirukkural is the classical Tamil text of ethics and conduct. Giving details about the event, Education Minister, Pralhad Joshi said that it will be inaugurated by Vice President CP Radhakrishnan on Saturday while the valedictory session will be attended by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. Mr Joshi said that around one thousand and 400  participants from Tamil Nadu, organised into seven groups of around 200 persons each, will undertake a visit to Varanasi, Prayagraj and Ayodhya as part of the programme.

Benchmark domestic equity indices ended over 1.8 per cent higher today with Sensex closing near 84 thousand mark. We have a report:

“The Sensex jumped 1 thousand 502 points to close at 83 thousand 938. The Nifty climbed 470 points to settle at 25 thousand 819. However, the broader market on the National Stock Exchange displayed a mixed trend. The Midcap 100 index gained 0.3 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index dipped over 0.4 per cent. In the forex market today, the rupee strengthened by 68 paise to close at 92 rupees and 23 paise against the US dollar.WITH DRISHTI’s Report, LALIMA ANEJA DANG FOR AKASHVANI News.“

In bullion market today, gold and silver prices were hovering around 15-month low driven by a stronger US dollar and expectations of an interest rate hike by Federal Reserve. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold declined 3.1 per cent to 1 lakh 21 thousand 38 rupees per 10 grams.

In Hockey, Host India defeated Japan,4-Nil in the final league-stage match of the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal this evening. Indian women’s team has topped the group stage of the tournament and have already secured their place in the semifinals. Meanwhile, the Indian women’s Hockey team has climbed to 4th place in the FIH rankings, its highest-ever position since the world body introduced the system in October 2003.

The Shiromani Akali Dal has rejoined the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. The Bharatiya Janata Party and the Shiromani Akali Dal will contest the upcoming polls together, with both parties expressing commitment to Punjab’s development and progress. The announcement was made by senior BJP leader and Home Minister Amit Shah at the party headquarters in New Delhi today.

 

Speaking to media, Shiromani Akali Dal President Sukhbir Singh Badal said, whenever the two parties have formed governments together, Punjab has witnessed progress, peace, stability and communal harmony.

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has expressed happiness over the Shiromani Akali Dal rejoining the National Democratic Alliance. In a social media post, Mr Modi said, the alliance was a natural partnership that will ensure people-centric governance in Punjab and take the state to new heights of progress. He also expressed confidence that the alliance would emerge as the preferred choice of the people of Punjab.

 

<><><> 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz today reviewed the progress of their Strategic Partnership and expressed satisfaction over the continued momentum in bilateral engagements. Mr Modi received a telephone call from the German Chancellor today. As India and Germany mark 75 years of diplomatic relations this year, the two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening cooperation across key sectors, including defence, trade and investment, and advanced technologies. They noted that the India-EU Free Trade Agreement will open up new opportunities for expanding bilateral trade and investment. Mr Modi and Mr Merz agreed to continue working closely to promote global peace, stability and a rules-based international order.

Communications Minister Jyotiraditya M. Scindia said, India has transformed from a consumer of technology into a creator of technology over the past decade. Mr Scindia was addressing the Telecom Startups and MSME Conclave 2026 in New Delhi today. The Minister said India now has more than two lakh startups, a growth driven by several initiatives undertaken the NDA government of the past decade. Highlighting the growth of digital connectivity, the Minister said India currently has around 110 crore internet connections and 104 crore broadband connections. He also emphasised that India is the only telecom market in the world witnessing double-digit growth.

 

<><><> 

 

Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said, India’s space economy, currently valued at nearly 9 billion US dollars, is projected to grow to 40 to 45 billion US dollars in less than a decade. The Minister was addressing the fifth India International Space Conclave 2026 in New Delhi today. Dr Singh said the establishment of NewSpace India Limited, followed by the creation of IN-SPACe and the opening up of the space sector to private participation, marked a major transformation in India’s space journey. Referring to the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan, the Minister said space-based applications help improve infrastructure planning and ensure timely project completion.

Celebrations of Guru Nanak Jayanti and Dev Deepawali on Kartik Purnima drew large numbers of devotees to gurdwaras and temples across the country today.

 

Guru Nanak Jayanti, also known as Gurpurab and Parkash Purab, is being celebrated across the country and around the world with great religious fervour and devotion. The occasion marks the 557th birth anniversary of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the founder of Sikhism.

 

Guru Nanak Dev Ji was born in 1469 on Kartik Purnima, the full moon day of the lunar month of Kartik. His teachings of oneness, equality, compassion and selfless service continue to inspire millions across the world.

 

Gurdwaras across the country, including the Golden Temple in Amritsar, have been beautifully decorated with lights and flowers to mark the auspicious occasion. In Delhi, devotees are thronging historic gurdwaras to offer prayers and participate in special kirtan programmes.

 

“Processions and prayers marked Gurpurab – the birth anniversary of  Guru Nanak Dev in Delhi. Lakhs of devotees thronged historic Gurdwaras in the national capital including Bangla Sahib, Sis Ganj, Rakab Ganj, Nanak Piao, Damdama Sahib and Gurudwara Bala Sahib since morning and offered prayers. Early morning processions, also known as prabhat pheris were taken out by gurdwaras across the city carrying flags and singing devotional songs. Akhand Path and free community langar were also organised to mark the occasion. On the eve of Guru Nanak Jayanti yesterday , Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended a Shabad Kirtan at Lok Niwas hosted by Delhi Lieutenant Governor. Today Vice President C P Radhakrishnan visited Gurudwara Rakab Ganj Sahib and offered prayers. ANUPAM MISHRA, AKASHVANI NEWS, DELHI.”

 

On the auspicious occasion of Kartik Purnima, people across the country took holy dips in rivers, while the holy city of Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh witnessed Dev Deepawali celeberations, also known as the Festival of Lights of the Gods, this evening. Our correspondent has the details:
 

“Tourism and Culture Minister of state Jaiveer Singh inaugurated the celebrations by lighting a ceremonial lamp at Namo Ghat. Around 11 lakh earthen lamps illuminated all 84 ghats of Kashi, while the traditional Ganga Aarti was performed on various ghats. Lakhs of devotees and tourists from across the country and abroad reached Varanasi to witness the grand celebrations. A spectacular 3D projection mapping and laser show a grand display featuring 2,100 indigenous drones was also organised. Dev Deepawali celebrations were also organised along the banks of the Mandakini River in Chitrakoot and at the banks of major rivers in several other cities across the state. SUSHIL CHANDRA TIWARI AAKASHWANI NEWS LUCKNOW .”

 

The President, Vice President and Prime Minister extended their greetings to the people on the occasion of Parkash Purab and Dev Deepawali.

President Droupadi Murmu has said, despite global uncertainties and financial instability, India’s steady progress reflects the country’s commitment towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat. The President was speaking after inaugurating the historic Bali Jatra festival at Cuttack in Odisha this evening. She said the festival is one of Asia’s largest open-air annual trade fairs and celebrates Odisha’s glorious ancient maritime heritage. The annual festival in Odisha begins on Kartik Purnima, celebrated today with the traditional Boita Bandana ritual, in which people set afloat miniature boats to commemorate the state’s glorious maritime heritage and its ancient trade links with Southeast Asian countries.

 

At the venue, the President opened the ‘Cuttack in Cuttack’ theme pavilion. This year’s Bali Jatra, will continue for eight days until 1st of December.

The International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa today witnessed a diverse line-up of films and engaging masterclasses captivating film enthusiasts. The screenings and interactive sessions offered movie buffs an opportunity to explore different aspects of cinema and learn from industry experts. Meanwhile, five-day WAVES Film Bazaar, marking two decades of connecting Indian cinema with the global film industry, concluded at the festival today. It provided a platform for filmmakers, producers, writers, investors and distributors from India and abroad to exchange ideas, develop film projects and explore opportunities for international collaboration.

 

“Various film makers spoke about their films today. Mohammadreza Ardalan who is the Director of Iranian film ‘Poultry Farm’ told how his film explores vulnerability of undocumented children. Filmmaker Akhil Sathyan of movie Sarvam Maya said humour can draw audiences into a story and make its emotional moments more affecting. A restored version of Bhalji Pendharkar’s Marathi film Sadhi Manase was screened at the IFFI today. At the inaugural edition of Prasar Bharati’s Script Pitching Lab, ‘Page Se Pitch Tak’. Avishesh Jha won the first prize Satya Vyas secured the Silver Award, while Jitesh Thakur won the Bronze. The five-day WAVES Film Bazaar 2026 concluded today. Additional Secretary, Shri Prabhat highlighted global networking, co-production and  financing opportunities coming due to film bazaars. Mahesh Chopade Akashvani News Panaji.”

London School of Economics and Political Science, Delhi School of Economics and the Institute of Economic Growth signed Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in New Delhi in the presence of Vice President CP Radhakrishnan. Speaking at the event, the Vice President said, the agreement aims to strengthen academic collaboration and the sharing of knowledge.

Maldivian Foreign Minister Iruthisham Adam arrived in New Delhi today to participate in the 25th IORA Council of Ministers Meeting. The 25th Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) Meeting of the Council of Ministers will be held in New Delhi on Friday.

The European Union (EU) and the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) held their first-ever high-level roundtable on maritime security in New Delhi today. Representatives from countries across the Indian Ocean region discussed ways to strengthen maritime domain awareness, combat piracy and trafficking, and enhance cooperation to safeguard critical sea lanes. Addressing the gathering, EU Ambassador to India Jean-Eric Paquet said the European Union was ready to intensify cooperation and joint efforts with regional partners to tackle maritime crime in the Indian Ocean.

In Sports, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi created history by smashing the world record for the fastest century and double century in List A cricket as India ‘A’ defeated the United Arab Emirates by seven wickets in a group stage match of the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament at Doha in Qatar. Chasing a target of 250 runs set by the UAE, India ‘A’ comfortably reached the target in just 14.2 overs for the loss of three wickets. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said, India’s growth story is creating new opportunities and called upon Indian industries to be prepared to seize them. Mr Modi was addressing the gathering on centenary convention of industry body Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi today. The Prime Minister said FICCI has witnessed significant achievements in India’s industrial sector over the past 100 years. 

 

 

The Prime Minister said India is now the world’s fastest-growing major economy, with a projected growth rate of around seven per cent. He said the latest World Bank report, which states that 50 crore Indians have overcome poverty in just 12 to 13 years, is a matter of great pride for the nation.

 

 

Speaking at the event, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said that Viksit Bharat 2047 is not merely another agenda or target, but a collective national resolve driven by the energy and contribution of every Indian.

Home Minister Amit Shah has said, the country is now moving towards establishing a coordinated system to combat terrorism. He said, the government is building a system in which all police stations across the country will work on a unified strategy to combat terrorism. Mentioning the recent elimination of Lashkar terrorist Latif Bhat, Mr Shah said, the entire Kashmir has become free from terrorism. He said, this situation has come about after 35 years.

External Affairs Minister Dr S. Jaishankar and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh co-chaired the fourth Foreign and Defence Ministers’ (2+2) Dialogue with their Japanese counterparts Toshimitsu Motegi and Shinjiro Koizumi in Tokyo today. During the meeting, the two countries agreed to fast-track defence agreements related to the Unified Complex Radio Antenna (UNICORN) stealth naval mast project. The move aims to strengthen maritime security cooperation and expand joint defence manufacturing between the two countries.

 

 

 

Addressing a joint press briefing, Mr Singh said the discussions covered a wide range of issues under the two countries’ Special Strategic and Global Partnership.

 

 

Dr Jaishankar said cooperation between India and Japan aims to promote a multipolar Asia and a multipolar world.

 

 

Later, in a joint statement, both countries unequivocally and strongly condemned terrorism and violent extremism in all its form and manifestations, including cross-border terrorism, and called for action against all United Nations-listed terrorist groups and entities.

Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan over Bay of Bengal is moving north-northwestwards. It is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, passing close to the east of Gopalpur, by tomorrow noon. The India Meteorological Department said the cyclone has been moving at a speed of 13 kilometres per hour over the past six hours. Wind speeds at the time of landfall are expected to reach 90 to 100 kilometres per hour, with gusts of up to 110 kilometres per hour. Odisha and Andhra Pradesh governments have stepped up their preparedness to deal with the impending cyclone. In Odisha, more than one lakh five thousand people have already been evacuated to safer locations. Our correspondent has the details

 

 

 

“As a precautionary measure, the state government has already started the evacuation process in view of the impending cyclone. The government has set up over nine thousand shelters and deployed over 3 hundred emergency response teams, including NDRF and ODRAF, across vulnerable places in several districts. As of now, over 1 lakh 5 thousand people have been evacuated and shifted to safer places. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said the government is making all necessary preparations, with priority being given to ensure “zero casualties”. The Puri Shree Jagannath Temple Administration urged devotees to plan their visits in line with weather advisories in view of the Cyclonic storm. In view of Cyclone Akvan, Indian Railways has cancelled and rescheduled train services. With SN Patnaik this is Smrutirekha for Akashvani News Cuttack.”

 

 

 

The Andhra Pradesh Government has also intensified its preparations to tackle the approaching cyclone. More from our correspondent:

 

 

 

“Heavy rainfall is likely in parts of Srikakulam district. Moderate rain may occur in Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram Manyam, Alluri Sitarama Raju, Polavaram, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli and Kakinada districts. Strong winds may uproot trees and damage temporary structures. Low-lying areas may also face waterlogging. The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority has advised fishermen not to venture into the sea. People living along the North Andhra coast have been asked to remain alert. Farmers have been advised to protect harvested paddy from rain and follow official advisories. Allu Murali Akashvani News,Vijaywada.”

 

 

 

Under the influence of Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan, several districts of West Bengal are also experiencing rainfall.

The Government has revised the validity period of Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificates for different categories of vehicles. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has amended the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, in this regard. According to a Gazette notification, the validity of PUC certificates will now depend on the vehicle’s emission standards, category and age.

 

 

“Under the amended rules, vehicles complying with BS-I, BS-II and BS-III emission norms will have a PUC certificate valid for three months, while vehicles complying with BS-IV norms will have a validity of six months. For non-transport vehicles complying with BS-VI emission norms, the certificate will be valid for three years for vehicles up to six years old. While for vehicles more than six years and up to ten years old, the validity will be for one year. For vehicles older than ten years, the validity will be six months. In the case of transport vehicles complying with BS-VI norms, the certificate validity for vehicles up to six years old will be for two years. The validity of the certificate will be one year for vehicles of more than six years and up to ten years old, and six months for vehicles older than ten years. Akshit Vaidyan for Akashvani News, Delhi”

The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 is all set to begin in Goa tomorrow. We have a report:

 

 

“Goa is all set to host the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026, with preparations in place to welcome filmmakers, artists and cinema enthusiasts from across the world. The opening day will feature the screening of the film, ‘Fatherland’, directed by Polish filmmaker Paweł Pawlikowski. The film will be be screened at INOX Panjim from 2 PM, ahead of the grand opening ceremony at 5 PM at the Dr Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Indoor Stadium in Goa. Among the major additions this year are the two new sections, Films About Films and the Animation segment. Introduced for the first time in IFFI’s history, ‘Films About Films’ will feature five international productions exploring the lives, creative journeys and legacies of filmmakers, actors and cinema itself. While the Animation segment will present five acclaimed films from Japan, France, China, Singapore and the United States, highlighting the artistic possibilities and emotional depth of animated storytelling. The festival will also feature special showcases of Indian and international cinema, including a focus on BRICS films. Furthermore, Spain has been named the Country of Honour, while Russia will participate as the Partner Country. With Nikhil Upadhyay this is Vishnu from Goa”.
